Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR adds PostgreSQL runtime storage, bidirectional database ports, and matched backups for Logbook. **Example:** An operator selects database.engine: postgres and ports an existing Logbook installation. - **Before:** Logbook continues using SQLite and is unavailable to the PostgreSQL port provider. - **After:** Logbook metadata uses PostgreSQL while frame JPEGs remain at their existing file paths. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful shared-owner implementation with meaningful SQL coverage, but the missed production pruning envelope blocks correctness and existing-installation compatibility remains unproven. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Operators selecting PostgreSQL cannot currently use it for Logbook metadata, ports, or matched backups. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction follows the existing database-family rollout and preserves the SQLite default and local frame artifacts. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** Keep this PR open: it adds useful, maintainer-directed PostgreSQL support, but the production pruning path bypasses required write admission. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381` ## Before merge - [ ] **Route retention pruning through the engine write envelope (P2)** - With PostgreSQL selected, every pruneFrames command now requests transaction admission here, but LogbookStore.pruneFrames still calls this.worker.execute directly at store.ts:246. It therefore omits runEngineStoreOperation's write-admission factory, and the broker's default handler rejects the request with 'SQLite domain operation requires its own admission'. Scheduled retention cannot remove expired frames, even though the direct-backend test passes with admission mocked. Keep the frame-I/O queue and dispatch pruning through executeWorker. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Route retention pruning through the engine write envelope — `extensions/logbook/src/store.worker.ts:673-675` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Add real-broker PostgreSQL pruning coverage that fails on the reviewed head, and supply a latest-stable upgrade/port run preserving settings, rows, allocation marks, and frame files.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Logbook service sends capture, analysis, timeline, and retention operations to its worker; the shared database engine selects SQLite or PostgreSQL, while the family provider supplies port and backup contracts. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Logbook service] --> B[Logbook store] B --> C[Worker broker and admission] C --> D[Logbook SQL owner] D --> E[SQLite or PostgreSQL] D --> F[Frame JPEG files] G[Database port and backup] --> E ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep all Logbook writes, including retention pruning, under the existing engine-operation admission owner. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes the failure: PostgreSQL pruning reaches a transaction-admission request through a direct worker call whose default broker admission refuses domain writes; no target code was executed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing the existing engine and family-provider contracts is appropriate, but pruning must use the same host envelope as the other PostgreSQL writes. Full review comments: - [P2] Route retention pruning through the engine write envelope — `extensions/logbook/src/store.worker.ts:673-675` With PostgreSQL selected, every pruneFrames command now requests transaction admission here, but LogbookStore.pruneFrames still calls this.worker.execute directly at store.ts:246. It therefore omits runEngineStoreOperation's write-admission factory, and the broker's default handler rejects the request with 'SQLite domain operation requires its own admission'. Scheduled retention cannot remove expired frames, even though the direct-backend test passes with admission mocked. Keep the frame-I/O queue and dispatch pruning through executeWorker. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.96 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [12ec309f9b0b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/12ec309f9b0ba17ddc227451d896f70c956d2f48). ### Provenance checked - `Worker ownership and frame-operation ordering` keeps the original intent (8e7d9dd401bb69fba7fb55b8ff66fa9714f0cd59: Move SQL off the application thread while retaining capture, preview, pruning, and shutdown ordering.) - `Schema admission reuse` keeps the original intent (bb7d32e55d48a85c6a08b374064e7a45d1e52b9c: Reuse physical-database admission across handles and worker reopens instead of repeating schema validation.) - `Sampled-frame selection` keeps the original intent (0b68857e50bf1491c8046b12de4991d3fbcfa59c: Select the same chronological sample in one SQL statement while transferring less metadata.) - `Engine selection and family dispatch` keeps the original intent (d6f6f76abbe0e62ed38c43095f7f2d0209521d48: Provide one lazy family registry for database ports, discovery, and matched PostgreSQL backups.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres -- extensions/logbook/src/postgres-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - pnpm test extensions/logbook/src/store.test.ts extensions/logbook/src/store-frame-io.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - git diff --check What I checked: - **Current main still lacks Logbook PostgreSQL selection:** Fetched main opens Logbook with no database engine input and registers Logbook without PostgreSQL support. ([`src/infra/database-engine/registry.ts:16`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/12ec309f9b0ba17ddc227451d896f70c956d2f48/src/infra/database-engine/registry.ts#L16), [12ec309f9b0b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/12ec309f9b0ba17ddc227451d896f70c956d2f48)) - **Pruning misses the new host write envelope:** LogbookStore.pruneFrames calls worker.execute directly instead of executeWorker, which supplies runEngineStoreOperation and PostgreSQL write admission. ([`extensions/logbook/src/store.ts:246`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381/extensions/logbook/src/store.ts#L246), [c97723239030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381)) - **The broker rejects the missed admission:** Without a caller-supplied admission factory, the broker installs an admission handler that throws 'SQLite domain operation requires its own admission'; the new PostgreSQL worker requests transaction admission before pruning. ([`src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-reply.ts:161`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381/src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-reply.ts#L161), [c97723239030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381)) - **Runtime tests bypass the affected integration:** The PostgreSQL suite invokes createSqliteWorkerBackend directly and mocks requestSqliteWorkerOperationAdmission, so its successful pruning assertion cannot detect the missing LogbookStore envelope. ([`extensions/logbook/src/postgres-store.test.ts:14`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381/extensions/logbook/src/postgres-store.test.ts#L14), [c97723239030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381)) - **Meaningful port and backup coverage:** The added fixture exercises real PostgreSQL materialization, reverse porting, backup and restore, exact retained rows, all four deleted-maximum allocation marks, and unchanged frame paths and bytes. ([`src/infra/database-engine/logbook-port.postgres.test.ts:101`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381/src/infra/database-engine/logbook-port.postgres.test.ts#L101), [c97723239030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c9772323903078038707eaac9897cfa826d0b381)) - **Existing family-provider direction:** The merged prerequisite explicitly identifies Logbook as a subsequent consumer of the generic family registry: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172677. ([`src/infra/database-engine/port-provider.ts:14`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d6f6f76abbe0e62ed38c43095f7f2d0209521d48/src/infra/database-engine/port-provider.ts#L14), [d6f6f76abbe0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d6f6f76abbe0e62ed38c43095f7f2d0209521d48)) ### PR surface Source +342, Tests +485, Docs +7, Config 0, Generated +453, Other +72. Total +1359 across 25 files. Added test files: 2.
View PR surface stats | Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Source | 14 | 536 | 194 | +342 | | Tests | 5 | 487 | 2 | +485 | | Docs | 1 | 16 | 9 | +7 | | Config | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | | Generated | 1 | 453 | 0 | +453 | | Other | 3 | 73 | 1 | +72 | | **Total** | **25** | **1566** | **207** | **+1359** |
### Labels Label changes: - add `P2`: This is an opt-in storage improvement with a concrete PostgreSQL retention defect and limited blast radius. - add `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - add `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. Label justifications: - `P2`: This is an opt-in storage improvement with a concrete PostgreSQL retention defect and limited blast radius. - `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. Comment `@clawsweeper re-review` for a fresh review only. Repair and merge execution lanes are retired.
